The digital version of a driver's license added to iPhone appears to be rolling out soon in the 15th U.S. state.

Apple currently lists 14 states that support the feature, along with the territory of Puerto Rico, and backend assets now indicate that another state will soon be added...

Many people have long hoped to avoid carrying physical identification documents, such as driver's licenses and passports, and instead simply use an iPhone or Apple Watch to present digital ID.

That vision may still have a long way to go, but Apple took the first step in 2021 when the company announced plans to allow iPhone users to add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. So far, 14 states have adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend assets discovered by MacRumors indicate that Oklahoma will soon be added to the list.

We previously detailed the steps for adding a driver's license or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. As noted at the time, please note that the digital ID cannot fully replace the physical document, so unfortunately we still recommend that you continue to carry the physical version with you.

Even so, the digital version can still help protect your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints, as well as when you need to prove your age to a merchant. The ID will only confirm that you meet the age requirement, without disclosing any personal information, such as your date of birth.
